correctness.rationale: For h>=2 and n>=3h every indexed three-one word has exactly three marked initial markers; each marked representation consists of a position i and an ordered positive gap triple (a,b,c)>=h with sum n. The checksum is 3i+2a+b mod n, with exactly Q=binom(n-3h+2,2) gap triples. When 3 is invertible mod n each residue gets Q marked descriptions, hence Q/3 words. When 3 divides n there are three solutions for i exactly when 2a+b matches the residue mod 3, canceling the three markings. A primitive cubic root-of-unity evaluates the weighted composition generating function to 1/(1-z^3), yielding counts (Q+2)/3 and (Q-1)/3 in the respective mod-three classes. The boundary n=3h is included. The extracted standalone verifier independently enumerated 247 (n,h) pairs for n<=42 and passed; finitary tests are supporting only.

value.rationale: Constrained moment balance is a motivated quantity in synchronization-error coding research, already emphasized by Cheng et al. (2010). For the smallest three-marker circular sparse family and every nontrivial minimum cyclic spacing, the complete checksum class distribution has a sharp arithmetic two-regime law and integer-optimal discrepancy zero or one. This is a complete exact infinite-family count with actionable balanced-bucket sizes, rather than an arbitrary numerical example or an implication of a general code-size bound. It makes no unsupported claim of error-correction power.
